texts: Language bricks
We normally use simple present tense to talk about places and where they are.
Statements
Questions
Negative statements
The park is on the Main Avenue.
IS the park on the Main Avenue? / Where is the park?
The park is not on the Main Avenue.
The public library is in front of the bank; so, take the train downtown.
How do I get to the public library?
I am not sure, Do you know where is it?
To get to the Caffe, go along the park.
Do you have to go across the park to get to the Caffe?
You don’t have to go between the park and local market to get to the Caffe.
The restaurant is opposite to the bakery.
Where is the restaurant?
The restaurant is not next to the bakery; it is opposite.
TO CONSIDER
- Prepositions are used to indicate location.
- Downtown does not use any preposition: I am going downtown.
- More than 1 verb can be used to talk about directions. / Questions vary too.

texts: Functional English
Language Targets
Aspects
Examples
Ask for directions.
Where  is the park? / How do I get to the bank? / Is the Caffe across the street?
State where a place is.
I think the public library is along the main avenue on Jefferson Street’s corner.
Explain how to get to a place.
You have to take the number 10 bus, get off at the West park, walk 1 block and you find the bank.
When we talk about places, we can consider the following aspects.
TO CONSIDER
Prepositions are essential to work with these 3 aspects since they state locations and placement.

texts: We are lost, right?
So, We are lost, Annie!
No, we are not, Nathan. See¡ we are on Maple Street.
And? We are supposed to be on K-Street at the museum.
Well, we are close, look! We need to walk two blocks and go along the park.
And then? Is the museum across the park?
No! we get out of the park and go left for one block and we get to K-Street.
But are you sure? I don’t want to get lost.
Don’t worry! The museum is on the first right corner of K-Street.
Ok, let’s go.
C. Read the following dialogue and state if the sentences are true (T) or false (F). After that, read the dialogue aloud with your teacher.
1. They are on the main avenue.	     (T) (F)
2. They need to be on K-Street.	     (T) (F)
3. They need to go to the local market.  (T) (F)
4. They have to walk three blocks.          (T) (F)
5. They have to go along the park. 			          (T) (F)
6. They have to go left when they get out of the park.  (T) (F)
7. Annie is not sure about the information.		          (T) (F)
8. The museum is on the first right corner of K-Street. (T) (F)
